Built upon a pulsing drone, the song starts quietly and then increases in intensity, the drums pounding harder as it builds to a breathless climax. Balkan folk meets hypnotic post-punk Singer Sveltlana Spajič says: "This song attempts to describe an epileptic seizure. Some friends said it sounded as though Đorđe Marković Koder had written it — a Serbian poet remembered for his strange language, invented words, and private mythology." #gordan #experimental #folk #krautrock

media:group.media:title: BaBa ZuLa - XXX - OUT NOW
media:group.media:description:
🌀 Three decades into their extraordinary journey, the legendary Istanbul-based collective BaBa ZuLa return with a new album!
🎶 The album moves through dreamlike narratives, social commentary and contemporary mythologies. Pulsating rhythms, transformed saz textures, analogue electronics and hypnotic grooves create a space where reality and imagination dissolve into one another. By turns playful, visionary and fiercely political, they draw connections between folklore, urban life, ecology, memory and resistance, grounding the album’s sonic adventures in a deeply human narrative.🔮✊🌿🧿

media:group.media:title: Gordan - Mara (official audio video)
media:group.media:description:
The first single from Gordan's upcoming album Gastarbeiter (out November 20, 2026) Listen: https://idol-io.ffm.to/mara
A timeless deep Balkan lament about the absurdities of modernity. Swinging bass and drum repetitions punctuated by ambient feedback and noise and Svetlana Spajić's folk inspired vocals. As if Joy Division had collaborated with a soloist from the Bulgarian Women's choir. Spajić tells us: "the entire song evolved from one funny folk-style couplet about a woman named Mara stranded on the German Autobahn in her new car with no money, sending word back to her man in the Balkans to rescue her."

entry.title: Oman Bagpipe Singers: Songs of returning and leaving (teaser)

media:group.media:title: Oman Bagpipe Singers: Songs of returning and leaving (teaser)
media:group.media:description: Pre-save the album: https://idol-io.ffm.to/omanbagpipesingerssongsofreturningandleaving Listen: https://idol-io.ffm.to/theboyhasjustarrivedfromeastafricadoesntknowhowtospeakarabic In Oman, descendants of the African slave trade live in the port district that hosts the country's principal harbor. Musicians performing Al-Mudema (“sailor songs”) in this neighborhood continue to sing primarily in Swahili, preserving a centuries-old musical tradition that blends African rhythms with the sounds of bagpipes and conch shells. This album features recordings made by Grammy Award–winning producer Ian Brennan (Tinariwen, Ustad Saami) in Oman of two Al-Mudema groups— Al Ajial (“Generations”) and Al Khair (“Imported Goods”). The session was recorded outdoors on the beach. Both ensembles consisted of eight core members, all of whom, except the players of the qurbah (bagpipe) and jem (conch shell), contributed vocals and various forms of percussion, including the majur, a waist-worn belt made from goat hooves.

entry.title: Širom - Curls Upon the Neck, Ribs Upon the Mountain (Official Video)

media:group.media:title: Širom - Curls Upon the Neck, Ribs Upon the Mountain (Official Video)
media:group.media:description:
Taken from the album "In the Wind of Night, Hard-Fallen Incantations Whisper" (03 October 2025 tak:til, Glitterbeat Records) https://idol-io.ffm.to/inthewindofnighthardfallenincantationswhisper
To create the video for their track Curls Upon the Neck, Ribs Upon the Mountain, Širom enlisted the Slovenian filmmaker Tit Brecelj, making it a continuation of the collaboration they started with the 2017 documentary film Širom - Memoryscapes.
For the theme of the video, Širom envisioned capturing people performing ancient crafts, tasks that have been carried out for centuries, linked by manual labour and a deep harmony with the natural world. Set against the dusk of summer evenings, Tit filmed Primož Bizjan stoking a fire and Sebastjan Gršak forging metal. By embracing both intuition and spontaneity, the team produced an evocative film that resonates surprisingly with the title of their forthcoming album "In the Wind of Night, Hard-Fallen Incantations Whisper".
Curls Upon the Neck, Ribs Upon the Mountain draws upon the trio’s individual and collective experiences and thoughts. The homemade bass harp and the Mongolian stringed instrument morin khuur, which Širom are using for the first time, emerge strong from the intricate instrumental mosaic. The whisper is faint within the interplay of the band’s formidable array of instruments; but once you hear it, it cannot remain unheard.

media:group.media:description:
Taken from In the Wind of Night, Hard-Fallen Incantations Whisper (out October 3, 2025 on tak:til) preorder: https://idol-io.ffm.to/inthewindofnighthardfallenincantationswhisper
‘For You, This Eve, the Wolves Will Be Enchantingly Forsaken’ was created from two musical ideas. The first arose from creative interplay within the group, the second from Samo’s studies of the harmonium. Both factors were also at play in the music created for the Dodekalogija 1972–1983 theatre performance.
With its linear composition, its piercing, repetitive rhythm section of percussion and morin khuur, and Samo’s towering vocals and uplifting harmonies, the track envelops the whole album in ecstasy and optimism.

entry.title: The Good Ones - Rwanda Sings With Strings - album teaser

media:group.media:title: The Good Ones - Rwanda Sings With Strings - album teaser
media:group.media:description:
Taken from the upcoming album Rwanda Sings With Strings (Glitterbeat Records 29 Aug 2025) Pre-orders: https://idol-io.ffm.to/rwandasingswithstrings
For the fifth album by Rwandan duo The Good Ones, the group's producer, Ian Brennan (Tinariwen, Ramblin’ Jack Elliott, Parchman Prison Project) scheduled a cellist and violinist to accompany them. The entire album was recorded in single takes without written scores or demos. The arrangements were improvised on the fly. Within minutes of meeting all four musicians were recording— the only communication musical.
The session fulfilled the group’s long-held dream to have main writer, guitarist, and lead vocalist Adrien Kazigira’s songs performed with strings. (percussionist/harmony vocalist Janvier Havugimana rounds out the lineup). Sequestered in a DC hotel room the day prior to The Good Ones duo’s Tiny Desk session taping, the musicians recorded nineteen songs in just three hours.
“It was all an experiment,” reports producer Ian Brennan, “But the second the strings entered during the first song, it felt like the room began levitating and there was no doubt that something magical and profoundly beautiful was occurring." The sound is steeped in a romanticism, longing, and sense of resigned grandeur that harkens back to African Balladeers such as Boubabcar Traore and Miriam Makeba, as well as Nick Drake, early Leonard Cohen, and Astral Weeks. Perfect Sunday morning listening.

media:group.media:title: Samba Touré - Wotoro Pousselaw (official video)
media:group.media:description:
Taken from Baarakelaw (out 24.01.2025 on Glitterbeat Records) Listen/buy now: https://idol-io.ffm.to/baarakelaw
Wotoro Pousseelaw - A deep slice of northern Malian magic. The calabash and shaker setting the rhythm, and Samba's plaintive, layered vocals and guitars entwining on top. A song to encourage the pousse-pousseurs (hand-cart drivers, literally push-pushers!). They are important workers in big Malian cities, transporting just about everything from one place to another: furniture when moving house, carpets and linen to be washed at the river, fruit and vegetables to sell... From morning to night, they push their trolleys everywhere in the middle of traffic, pollution and dust. They are very useful to everyone. Sung in mixed Bambara and Songhoy.

entry.title: Parchman Prison Prayer - Open the Floodgates of Heaven (Let It Rain)

media:group.media:title: Parchman Prison Prayer - Open the Floodgates of Heaven (Let It Rain)
media:group.media:description:
Taken from Another Mississippi Sunday Morning (out Jan 17, 2025 Glitterbeat Records) Listen/order: https://idol-io.ffm.to/anothermississippisundaymorning
The track “Open the Floodgates of Heaven (Let It Rain)” was recorded as a storm suddenly splattered and thundered mid-song. Singer J. Hemphill’s interpretation of the source material is so singular that it is unrecognizable as a cover. Now sixty-seven years old, Hemphill has been serving a Life sentence since his early-twenties. The tenderness in his voice should serve as undeniable proof alone for any parole hearing.

entry.title: Samba Touré - Assouma Kagne (official audio video)

media:group.media:title: Samba Touré - Assouma Kagne (official audio video)
media:group.media:description:
Taken from Baarakelaw (out 24.01.2025 on Glitterbeat Records) Pre-safe https://idol-io.ffm.to/baarakelaw
"Assouma Kagne" is the first single taken from the album and also the album's opening song. Slow-burning and with a seductive groove it is the song that encompasses all the others. All bar one of the songs on 'Baarakelaw' deal with a central theme: the trials and tribulations of those who work street jobs in a dusty, bustling West African city like Bamako. Sung in Bambara, the main local language in Mali, "Assouma Kagne" is dedicated to all the hard-working people who get up early to earn barely enough to feed their families every day. The street vendors, domestic help, itinerant dressmakers, water carriers.

entry.title: Parchman Prison Prayer - MC Hammer (official audio video)

media:group.media:title: Parchman Prison Prayer - MC Hammer (official audio video)
media:group.media:description:
Taken from "Another Mississippi Sunday Morning" (out January 17, 2025 on Glitterbeat Records) pre-order: https://idol-io.ffm.to/anothermississippisundaymorning
Whether one's a believer or not, this is an inescapably spiritual experience.” — UNCUT
The Parchman Prison Prayer’s debut album in 2023 was met with unexpected global acclaim, which lead Grammy-winning producer and author, Ian Brennan (Tinariwen, Zomba Prison Project, Ramblin’ Jack Elliott, The Good Ones [Rwanda]), return to Mississippi for a second time.
Twelve men participated for the second recording, ranging in age from 23 to 74. Three are serving life sentences and six of them were newer arrivals or not on the debut album. There were no guards or chaplains present this time.
All tracks were recorded in 100% live, first takes and without overdubs over the course of just a few hours. As with the first album, any and all artist proceeds benefit the prison chaplain program.

Video director: Suhas KS Rao DOP: Gotham Siddhart Editor & Colorist: Anup Simha Coreography: Sandhya Udupa Dancers: Punyashree Hegde Sanmathi Sandeep Abhignaa Jagirdar Madhushree Sankhya Atmankur
Saagara "3" is the third installment of an acclaimed collaboration between Polish producer/multi-instrumentalist Waclaw Zimpel (James Holden, Shackelton) and four virtuosic carnatic musicians from southern India - Giridhar Udupa (ghatam), Mysore N. Karthik (violin), Aggu Baba (khanjira) and K Raja (thavil).A buzzing juxtaposition of dense Indian rhythms and pulsating electronic patterns. An album of deeply transformative compositions that navigate tradition and experimentation as they move towards the universal. Some kindred reference points: Steve Reich, Sarathy Korwar, Talvin Singh, James Holden.
